doc.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013

title: Hampton band trumpeters and manager John Levy
summary: Lionel Hampton's trumpeters such as Eddie Williams encouraged him, and he recalls John Levy and the artists Levy managed.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Tomorrow. Tomorrow, for the marathon. I’d like to live there, at the Jenkins Orphanage in Charleston, South Carolina. A lot of people you know and love either went there or passed through. And Roy Eldridge used to stop by Daniel Jenkins all the time. Lionel Hampton had a trumpet player in the band, used to always send me messages. He’s way ahead of me by ten, eleven years. “Tell that boy to keep on playin’.” His name was Eddie Williams, the Lionel Hampton Band. He called himself “King Ed.” Because they really wanted me coming up through the ranks. Another trumpet player’s name was Monk. So they heard about me and they all passed away now, it breaks my heart. And that’s why when I come to see your room it represents so much more than just your room, than just your collection. It represents a whole lot more than what you have in here. John Levy and I were like this. I knew Joe Williams since 1961. Nancy Wilson, all of them. Ramsey Lewis, the girl that made “Street Life.” John Levy managed her too. Jazz Crusaders he managed.
Cannonball Adderley’s brother Nat. This brings back such deep memory for me. And Joe and Nancy were his prime people.
